title: Hold on a frame
goal: Sometimes the point of a recording is one frame: the result, the error, the final state. Let a frame be held on screen for as long as it needs, as an ordinary piece of the edit.
notes:
Build on docs/design/mocks/pages/video-freeze-wt.html, which states the design and the test in one line: "A freeze is not a special object: it is a clip whose in and out are the same frame, so it drops into the timeline like any other."

That is the check on the time model from the foundation task. If a held frame needs a special case, the model is wrong and that is worth saying rather than working around.

---
Grounded in the video clickthroughs, which the user says are ideas to build on rather than specs: say in the audit where you went further or differently and why. The thesis every page shares governs this too: video is not a mode, it is the layer document with time.
acceptance: A frame can be held for a chosen length, and it behaves on the timeline like any other piece: trim it, move it, put things over it
It is made from where the playhead is, in one move
Things can be drawn and animated over it, since pointing at the held frame is usually the reason for holding it
It exports as the frames it should be rather than as a still that stutters
Audit under queue/audits/ with a hold in a real edit, and anything rough filed as a follow-up
